HabiroCohomologyFoundations.summary: Nothing specific to q-Hodge or Habiro cohomology exists in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. Neither library has λ-rings, δ-rings or prisms, q-derivatives or q-de Rham complexes, animated rings, derived de Rham cohomology, décalage, q-Witt or de Rham–Witt complexes, Habiro-complete modules, or spectra. So HQ.2–HQ.6 and HQ.8 are unbuilt, HQ.1 is partly built only because its q-integer identities already exist, and HQ.7 is acceptance testing. What the libraries already have is generic support, all in Mathlib. The q-integer identities that HQ.1 calls prototype lemmas are there as geometric sums ([n]_q(q−1) = q^n − 1, Φ_p = [p]_q, Φ_p(1) = p). Mathlib also has p-typical Witt vectors with F, V and a ghost map (bijective only when p is invertible), Kähler differentials, underived filtrations, Tor, regular sequences, smooth and étale algebras, condensed and solid modules, and Fontaine's θ with B_dR⁺. HQ.1's local q-crystalline input duplicates PrismaticCohomology PR.6, HQ.2's derived de Rham/filtered/Lη/animation inputs duplicate DD.1–DD.2, AI.1 and EDS E5:animation, and HQ.5-trace restates RefinedTraceMethods RT.4:q-Hodge.

targets.target: q-integers [n]_q = ∑_{i<n} q^i with their interface identities: [n]_q·(q−1) = q^n − 1, [n]_1 = n and [p]_q = Φ_p(q), the generator of the q-prism ideal
targets.note: There is no separate name for [n]_q, but it is the geometric sum ∑_{i<n} X^i and these are its identities: `geom_sum_mul` holds in every ring, `Polynomial.cyclotomic_prime` identifies Φ_p with ∑_{i<p} X^i for p prime, `Polynomial.eval_one_cyclotomic_prime` gives Φ_p(1) = p, and `cyclotomic_prime_pow_eq_geom_sum` gives [p]_{q^{p^n}} = Φ_{p^{n+1}}. The 'prototype q-integer lemmas' therefore need no new mathematics. Mathlib's Pochhammer file still lists q-factorials, q-binomials and q-Pochhammer symbols as TODO.

targets.target: The q-derivative (Jackson operator) D_q f = (f(qx) − f(x))/((q−1)x) on polynomial algebras, with D_q(x^n) = [n]_q x^{n−1}
targets.note: Neither library has a q-difference or Jackson derivative operator. Only the q = 1 case exists: the ordinary `Polynomial.derivative` with d(X^n) = n·X^{n−1}. The substitution f(qx) can be written with `Polynomial.comp`, but the division by (q−1)x has not been constructed.

targets.target: The twisted Leibniz rule D_q(fg) = D_q(f)·g(qx) + f·D_q(g) and d∘d = 0 for the framed q-de Rham (q-difference) complex
targets.note: Neither library has a q-difference complex or a twisted derivation. A grep of both trees for q-derivative, q-difference, Jackson and q-de Rham found nothing.

targets.target: Specialisation of the framed q-de Rham complex at q = 1 to the ordinary algebraic de Rham complex
targets.note: Mathlib has Kähler differentials Ω¹_{B/A} with d: B → Ω¹ and the basis of Ω¹ for polynomial rings, but neither library has an algebraic de Rham complex (exterior powers of Ω¹ with a differential) or a specialisation map from a q-deformation. The only mention of de Rham in either tree besides B_dR is a remark in Mathlib/Data/Fin/Parity.lean.

targets.target: The local q-crystalline site, q-PD envelopes and the p-complete comparison of the framed q-de Rham complex with prismatic cohomology over the q-prism (ℤ_p[[q−1]], [p]_q), imported from PR.6
targets.note: Neither library has δ-rings, prisms, q-PD pairs or prismatic cohomology. The base ring ℤ_p[[q−1]] can be written as `PowerSeries` over `PadicInt`, and its ideal generator [p]_q = Φ_p(q) exists, but nothing about the prism exists.

targets.target: Global arithmetic gluing over a perfectly covered Λ-ring and its admitted algebras (Wagner Appendix A): combining the p-complete local constructions with rational de Rham data, framing independence through coherent comparison maps, and descent with cocycle identities
targets.note: Neither library defines λ-rings or Λ-rings (Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Dickson.lean:115 records that Mathlib does not know what a Lambda ring is), δ-rings, prisms or perfectly covered bases. `PerfectRing` exists only as the characteristic-p notion of a bijective Frobenius.

targets.target: Completed coefficient rings for the gluing, with convergence proofs instead of inverting q − 1
targets.note: Generic I-adic completion (`AdicCompletion`, `IsAdicComplete`) and formal power series exist. Missing are the specific (q−1)- and p-adically completed coefficient rings used in the gluing and the convergence statements for the glued differentials.

duplicates.note: PR.6 constructs the q-crystalline site, the framed q-de Rham complex, change of framing, cocycle descent and the p-complete comparison over (ℤ_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)). HQ.1 restates these as its local computations and owns only the global gluing.

targets.target: Animated (simplicial commutative) rings, polynomial resolutions, and derived q-de Rham qdR defined by sifted-colimit extension from polynomial algebras, with resolution independence and the construction before completion
targets.note: Mathlib has the categorical ingredients (simplicial objects, the class of sifted categories, left Kan extensions) but no animated rings, no polynomial-resolution functor and no derived q-de Rham. A grep for animated found nothing in either tree.

targets.target: Derived base change for qdR under its actual completion hypotheses
targets.note: There is no qdR, and no derived completion to base change along.

targets.target: Ordinary derived de Rham cohomology with its Hodge filtration and Hodge completion (imported from DD), specialised from qdR with the filtration
targets.note: Mathlib has Kähler differentials and the naive two-term cotangent complex of an extension. Neither library has the derived cotangent complex, derived exterior powers, derived de Rham or a Hodge filtration.

targets.target: Separation of ordinary tensor products from derived tensor products
targets.note: Mathlib has the ordinary `TensorProduct` and `CategoryTheory.Tor`, the left-derived functors of the tensor product in a monoidal abelian category with projective resolutions. Missing is a derived tensor product on `DerivedCategory` or for animated rings and modules.

targets.target: Complete filtered modules over the (q−1)-filtered coefficient ring, their associated graded, completion and filtered tensor products (from EnhancedDerivedSheaves)
targets.note: Mathlib has underived filtrations: `IsModuleFiltration`, I-filtrations with Artin–Rees (`Ideal.Filtration`), the categorical `FilteredObject` with strict morphisms, and I-adic completion. Missing are complete filtered objects in a derived or enhanced category, the associated-graded functor on them, filtered completion and filtered tensor products.

targets.target: The smooth underived q-de Rham complex qΩ versus derived qdR: Wagner Proposition 3.47 comparing qΩ with the q-Hodge completion of qdR and with Lη_{(q−1)} of qHdg
targets.note: Neither library has qΩ, qdR, q-Hodge completion or décalage.

targets.target: The décalage functor Lη with its torsion corrections, imported from AInfCohomology
targets.note: No Lη or décalage construction exists in either library; a grep for décalage/decalage found nothing.

targets.target: The derived de Rham specialisation with its filtration, the rational comparison, the separate p-completed rational comparison and the explicit diagram of completions and localisations
targets.note: Only the generic ring-level localisation and adic completion exist; none of the derived comparison squares does.

duplicates.note: DD.2 constructs derived de Rham from polynomial resolutions with its Hodge filtration, Hodge completion and filtered base change, which HQ.2 names as its q = 1 specialisation and import.
DD.1 builds the complete filtered enhanced modules, completed filtered tensor products, graded pieces and Hodge completion that HQ.2 asks to build (attributing them to EnhancedDerivedSheaves).
AI.1 constructs the generic décalage Lη_f with its torsion-removing cohomology formula, which HQ.2 imports for the Lη_{(q−1)} comparison.
E5:animation constructs animated commutative algebras, polynomial resolutions and sifted left Kan extensions, the resolution machinery HQ.2 uses to define qdR.

targets.target: Wagner's q-Hodge filtration (v2 Definition 1.6 / 3.2): a (q−1)-complete descending filtered object with degree-zero q-de Rham identification, filtered specialisation to the Hodge filtration, the rational and p-completed rational comparisons and the higher coherences
targets.note: Neither library has q-Hodge filtrations, q-de Rham objects or the Hodge filtration they specialise to; only the abstract `CategoryTheory.FilteredObject` exists.

targets.target: The q-Hodge modification qHdg: the (q−1)-completed colimit of fil⁰ → (q−1)fil¹ → (q−1)²fil² → ⋯
targets.note: Neither library has this construction, nor derived (q−1)-completion of a colimit of filtered pieces.

targets.target: Wagner Theorem 3.11: the functor on chosen q-Hodge-filtered inputs factors through the Habiro-complete category and is symmetric monoidal there, with finite products and base-change maps
targets.note: Mathlib has monoidal and braided functors between ordinary categories, but neither library has Habiro-complete modules (HabiroRings HR.2 is absent) or an enhanced symmetric monoidal structure.

targets.target: For each m ≥ 1, the exhaustive ascending filtration on qHdg/(q^m − 1) with graded pieces Σ^{−i} qW_m dR^i (derived m-truncated q-de Rham–Witt objects), with its maps and convergence
targets.note: Neither library has q-de Rham–Witt or de Rham–Witt objects; only degree-zero p-typical truncated Witt vectors exist.

targets.target: Lemma 3.3: no functorial q-Hodge section over all animated algebras, nor over all smooth algebras without localisation
targets.note: Not stated in either library.

targets.target: The positive-degree q-de Rham–Witt complex: differential, truncation sets, Frobenius and Verschiebung extensions and their relations (q-Witt v5 Definitions 3.1, 3.6, 3.9), without restriction maps
targets.note: Neither library has q-Witt vectors, q-de Rham–Witt complexes, big Witt vectors or truncation sets. Mathlib's F and V exist only on p-typical Witt vectors in degree zero.

targets.target: The ordinary de Rham–Witt complex with its genuine restriction maps (imported from CR.4), and the specialisations of the q-objects to it
targets.note: Mathlib has the degree-zero input: p-typical Witt vectors W(R) with Frobenius and Verschiebung, and truncated Witt vectors W_n(R). Missing are the positive-degree de Rham–Witt complexes W_nΩ^i with d, restriction, F, V and dlog, and any specialisation map from q-objects.

targets.target: Wagner q-Hodge v2 Corollary 3.31: the smooth derived-to-underived comparison of q-Witt differential forms, with all shifts
targets.note: Neither side of the comparison exists.

targets.target: Ghost-map injectivity under the actual torsion hypotheses (no definition by inverting ghost coordinates)
targets.note: Mathlib has the p-typical ghost map and proves it bijective when p is invertible in R. Missing are injectivity for p-torsion-free rings and any ghost map for q-Witt vectors.

targets.target: Compatible complexes over each cyclotomic completion, transition comparisons, and arithmetic fracture/descent to the Habiro coefficient ring under the source's completeness and connectivity hypotheses
targets.note: Neither library has cyclotomic completions of ℤ[q], Habiro rings or derived descent along them (HabiroRings HR.2–HR.3 and HabiroCyclotomicCompletions are unbuilt).

targets.target: Derived commutative-algebra descent only when the input carries the needed multiplicative coherences (no automatic E∞ upgrade)
targets.note: Neither library has E∞-algebras or derived commutative algebras.

duplicates.note: HR.4 owns the degree-zero q-Witt rings qW_m with Frobenius and Verschiebung, the ghost description under torsion hypotheses, and the absence of restriction maps; HQ.4 restates that operator discipline for the positive-degree extension.
CR.4 constructs the ordinary de Rham–Witt complexes W_nΩ with restriction, F, V and the torsion-qualified inversion of ghost coordinates, which HQ.4 imports and specialises to.

targets.target: Wagner Theorem 4.11: q-Hodge filtrations exist for smooth algebras over a perfectly covered Λ-ring A once every prime p ≤ the relative dimension is inverted
targets.note: Mathlib has smooth algebras (`Algebra.Smooth`), but neither library defines λ-rings or Λ-rings (Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Dickson.lean:115 records that Mathlib does not know what a Lambda ring is), δ-rings, prisms or perfectly covered bases.

targets.target: Corollary 4.16: partial-operad multiplicativity, with primes up to 2d inverted for products and the r·d bound for r-fold coherence
targets.note: Neither library has operads or E_n-type coherence data for these functors.

targets.target: Extension to smooth schemes by descent, and perfectness over the Habiro completion of the localised ring for smooth proper schemes
targets.note: Neither library has Habiro completions or q-Hodge cohomology of schemes.

targets.target: Quasi-regular inputs under condition (R): p-torsion-free, static p-completed derived de Rham, Hodge filtration given by ideals; quotients of étale algebras over perfect Λ-rings by Koszul-regular ideals
targets.note: Mathlib has regular and weakly regular sequences and étale algebras. Neither library has Koszul-regular ideals, derived de Rham cohomology or condition (R).

targets.target: Theorem 4.22 (regular sequence of powers x_i^{a_i}, a_i ≥ 2, or a spherical E₁-lift), Theorem 4.29's canonical section on its subcategory, and the uniqueness statements with finite-order comparisons or the ℤ_p^×-action
targets.note: Neither library has spectra or spherical lifts, and none of these theorems is stated.

targets.target: For finite étale number-field inputs: export of the completed cohomology object to HR.6, the q − 1 completion comparison and the Frobenius-glued Taylor maps
targets.note: Mathlib has rings of integers and polynomial Taylor expansion, but neither library has the number-field Habiro ring or Frobenius-glued Taylor maps (HabiroNumberFields HB.6 is unbuilt).

duplicates.note: HR.6 states the degree-zero identification of q-Hodge/Habiro cohomology for étale inputs, including the q − 1 completion comparison that HQ.5's number-field paragraph also asks to prove.

targets.target: Wagner (ku and q-de Rham) Theorem 1.2 / 4.27: q-Hodge filtrations for a quasi-syntomic ring R with 2 invertible and a connective spherical E₂-lift S_R with S_R ⊗ Hℤ ≃ HR, imported from RT.4:q-Hodge
targets.note: Neither library has spectra, ku, E₂-rings, quasi-syntomic rings or topological Hochschild homology. A grep for syntomic, Hochschild (other than a group-cohomology TODO) and E∞ found nothing.

targets.target: The separate p = 2 / E₁ refinement under its additional even-resolution hypotheses
targets.note: Not present in either library.

duplicates.note: RT.4:q-Hodge states the same Wagner Theorem 1.2 / 4.27 under the same hypotheses (quasi-syntomic, 2 invertible, connective spherical E₂-lift) with the same p = 2 / E₁ caveat; HQ.5-trace only imports it.

targets.target: A precise ring/complex/line-bundle comparison problem between the algebraic q-Hodge construction and Scholze's analytic Habiro framework, stated with explicit domain, coefficient change and expected natural transformation
targets.note: Mathlib has condensed modules and solid condensed modules, but neither library has analytic rings, analytic stacks or an analytic Habiro stack, so the comparison cannot yet be stated.

targets.target: Proofs of all algebraic specialisations and number-field comparisons of the q-Hodge theory
targets.note: These are the results of HQ.1–HQ.5, none of which exists.

targets.target: Comparison after an analytic completed localisation, and the relation of the root-of-unity infinitesimal theory to the algebraic q-de Rham–Witt specialisation
targets.note: Not present in either library.

targets.target: Acceptance examples: a one-variable polynomial ring, the q-integer differential at q = 1, a finite étale number-field ring, a smooth scheme with the required small primes inverted, and a 2-inverted trace input with an explicit spherical lift, each commuting with de Rham specialisation and the p-adic comparison
targets.note: These are tests of HQ.1–HQ.5. Only the q = 1 end of the second test has library content: the ordinary derivative d(X^n) = n·X^{n−1}.

targets.target: Checks that a filtered object differs from its colimit modification, that derived-limit/Tor corrections are retained, that tensor powers can leave the smooth existence category, and that Hodge-completed and uncompleted theories differ
targets.note: These are regression checks on unbuilt constructions; only the generic `CategoryTheory.Tor` exists.

targets.target: Executable q-difference signatures on the existing polynomial API (Suggested.lean), with no Prop placeholder or axiom for the q-Hodge conditions
targets.note: Mathlib's polynomial API (composition, derivative, geometric and cyclotomic sums) supports such signatures, but the q-difference operator itself is not defined (see HQ.1).

duplicates.note: HR.7 is the matching acceptance suite for the coefficient rings; its zero-dimensional cohomology comparison test overlaps HQ.7's finite étale number-field test.

targets.target: A map-level comparison atlas: for each square, the base prism or perfectoid base, the smooth/proper or quasi-syntomic hypotheses, the derived completion ideal, what is inverted, Frobenius linearisation, filtration and Tate/Breuil–Kisin twist
targets.note: None of the objects in the squares (q-Hodge, derived de Rham, de Rham–Witt, prismatic, AΩ) exists in either library.

targets.target: Commutation of the global arithmetic q-gluing and the q-Hodge modification with the DD, PR.6, CR.4, AInf and CP local comparison maps, on the intersection of their hypotheses
targets.note: Neither side of any of these squares exists.

targets.target: The q = 1, cyclotomic, crystalline and A_inf specialisations proved through those maps, with information-losing comparisons recorded as base changes or localisations
targets.note: Mathlib has the A_inf-side inputs: Fontaine's θ from W of the tilt (`PreTilt`) and B_dR⁺ for p-adically complete rings. Neither library has A_inf cohomology, crystalline cohomology or any q-de Rham object to specialise.

duplicates.note: PR.6 proves AΩ_R ≃ qΩ_{R/A_inf} ≃ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A_inf} (BS22 Theorem 17.2), the A_inf specialisation of q-de Rham cohomology that HQ.8 lists among its squares.
CP.1 proves commutativity of the integral comparison diagram (θ, θ̃, Witt, A_cris, μ-inversion, AΩ), the classical squares HQ.8's atlas must commute with.
RT.6 builds the trace-to-prismatic comparisons and records the same ordering (RT.6 before HQ.8), so the THH/Nygaard/syntomic squares of HQ.8 are its outputs.
